1.why: All 14 screenshots show a static, uncluttered layout with no pop-ups, modals, banners, or animated/moving imagery — only cards, text, and buttons.

2.why: Primary actions are solid dark-blue buttons, the current step chip is filled, and the blue guidance banner plus green success text draw the eye, though the 'Logs' technical panel competes for attention on every page.

3.why: Each screen presents a single task with a heading, one or two fields, and one main button, plus a persistent top nav (Password recovery / Secure sign-in / Privacy conditions), making the needed item easy to locate.

4.why: The 5-chip progress tracker and 'Next: ...' banner externalize the steps, though the user must still carry codes from the Logs panel into the input fields and remember the 12-character password rule.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or 'show password' toggle appears on any screen, including the sign-in page in steps 09–14.

6.why: Nothing is saved or pre-filled for recognition — no remembered email, masked account hint, or stored device; the only 'familiar' item is the raw simulated token in the Logs debug list.

7.why: Text is consistently short and plain, e.g. 'Start by requesting a recovery code. You can pause and return safely.' and 'Use 12 or more characters with uppercase, lowercase, a number, and a symbol.'

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the 14 screenshots — only green success messages — so the claim that error messages describe problem and fix cannot be substantiated.

9.why: Requirements are described in prose (password rule, 'Use the practice delivery token shown in Logs') but no field placeholders, sample values, or worked examples of what to type are shown.

10.why: The password and security-code steps are clearly labelled, but no alternative login options (face/biometric, passkey) exist, so 'choices such as password, code, or face login' are only partially present.

11.why: Each screen offers essentially one decision at a time — one field and one primary button — with no competing option sets.

12.why: Every action produces explicit feedback: 'A security code has been prepared for this practice session.', 'Password confirmed. Next, confirm your security code.', 'Privacy conditions accepted...', plus an appended Logs entry.

13.why: A collapsible 'Help and safe sign-in reminders' panel appears on every page and a 'Next: ...' hint banner precedes each new step, though the help text is identical rather than step-specific.

14.why: Fields remain editable, the buttons can be re-pressed (e.g. 'Send security code' again) and 'Forgot your password? Start recovery' is always available, but no explicit back/retry control or error-recovery path is visible.

15.why: Identical header, nav, step chips, card structure, button styling, help panel, and Logs panel repeat across all 14 screens.
